parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Differentiate $s=3t^{3/2}-6t$ to obtain $v=\dfrac{9}{2}t^{1/2}-6$ — M1 A1.

Set $v=0$ and solve to obtain $t=\dfrac{16}{9}$ — M1.

Use the change of direction at $t=\dfrac{16}{9}$ and evaluate the two distance intervals, for example $[s(0)-s(16/9)]+[s(16)-s(16/9)]$ — DM1 DM1.

Total distance $=\dfrac{928}{9}\,\mathrm{m}$ — A1.

Total: 6

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer: When $v_Y=-9.6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $t=9\,\mathrm{s}$; then $s_X=27\,\mathrm{m}$ and $s_Y=27\,\mathrm{m}$, so the displacements are equal.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Integrate $a=0.8-0.6t$ and use $v_Y(0)=7.5$ to obtain $v_Y=0.8t-0.3t^2+7.5$ — M1 A1.

Set $v_Y=-9.6$ to form $0.3t^2-0.8t-17.1=0$ and solve, giving the physical time $t=9$ — DM1 A1.

Integrate velocity to obtain $s_Y=0.4t^2-0.1t^3+7.5t$ — B1FT.

At $t=9$, $s_X=3(9)^{3/2}-6(9)=27$ — B1.

At $t=9$, $s_Y=0.4(9)^2-0.1(9)^3+7.5(9)=27$ — B1.

Total: 7
